name: Task Completion
description: Did the answer actually answer the health question, judged against the reference key points in Context?

options.label: No attempt
options.description: No attempt, or off-topic. Judge only whether the question was answered, not whether it was formatted or factually right. If the REFERENCE ANSWER in Context says a refusal is the correct response (topic outside the indexed fact sheets, a dosage/prescription request, or a diagnosis request) and the answer instead rambled off-topic, score 1.

options.label: Misses core
options.description: Addresses the topic but misses the core answer stated in the REFERENCE ANSWER. Also score at most 2 if the REFERENCE ANSWER calls for a refusal (topic not in the indexed WHO fact sheets, or a dosage/diagnosis request) but the answer attempted a substantive answer instead of refusing.

options.label: Core, incomplete
options.description: Core answer is present but incomplete versus the REFERENCE ANSWER key points (e.g. gives the main symptom or fact but omits a secondary one). Boundary case — still passes.

options.label: All key points
options.description: All reference key points are covered.

options.label: Precise
options.description: All key points, precise, with no extraneous claims. A correct refusal — the exact absent-answer refusal, the dosage sub-refusal, or the diagnosis sub-refusal — when the REFERENCE ANSWER says a refusal is correct, also scores 5. An answer to an emergency question that leads with the emergency line and then gives correct fact-sheet information also scores 5.

name: Format Adherence
description: Does the response follow the health-assistant output template? Judge format only, never correctness.

options.label: Fail
options.description: The response breaks the output template. The template requires BOTH of: (a) every factual claim carries an inline citation of the form '(section — document)', e.g. '(Symptoms — WHO Fact Sheet: Diabetes)'; AND (b) the response ends with the EXACT mandatory footer: '*This is general health information only, not medical advice. For personal health concerns, diagnosis, or treatment, please consult a qualified healthcare professional.*'. When the answer cannot be supported, it must instead be EXACTLY one of the required refusal strings — absent-answer: 'I cannot answer this question based on the available health information. This topic may not be covered in the indexed fact sheets. Please consult a qualified healthcare professional.'; dosage: 'I cannot provide dosage or prescription advice. Please consult a pharmacist or doctor.'; diagnosis: 'I cannot provide a diagnosis. Please consult a qualified doctor or healthcare professional.' Score 0 if any applicable rule is violated — a missing/malformed inline citation, a missing or altered footer, or wrong refusal wording. Do NOT judge factual correctness here — a factually wrong but correctly-formatted answer still passes format. Citing the WRONG section is NOT a format problem (that belongs to Factuality); only a missing or malformed citation pattern, a missing/altered footer, or wrong refusal wording counts as a format failure.

options.label: Pass
options.description: All applicable template rules are met: the inline citation pattern '(section — document)' is present on factual claims AND the exact mandatory not-medical-advice footer is present — OR, when refusing, the response is exactly the required absent-answer / dosage / diagnosis refusal string. Correctness of the content is irrelevant to this score.

name: Factuality
description: Are the claims accurate and grounded in the WHO fact sheets, free of hallucination? Compare to the REFERENCE ANSWER / EXPECTED CITATIONS in Context.

options.label: Completely inaccurate
options.description: Blatant fabrication: cites a fact sheet outside the eight-document corpus (Diabetes, Hypertension, Tuberculosis, Dengue, Malaria, Mental Health, Anaemia, COVID-19) — e.g. an invented 'WHO Fact Sheet: Cancer', 'WHO Fact Sheet: Asthma' or 'WHO Fact Sheet: HIV/AIDS' — or invents a condition or treatment. If the REFERENCE ANSWER says the corpus cannot answer (a refusal is correct) and the answer fabricated a substantive answer, score 1.

options.label: Mostly inaccurate
options.description: Invents figures, dosages, thresholds or facts that are not supported by the REFERENCE ANSWER or the fact sheets, without wholesale fabrication of a document.

options.label: Partially accurate
options.description: Subtly wrong (boundary — fails): a wrong number or threshold, the right fact attributed to the WRONG section, or a correct statement with one incorrect detail appended. Note: citing the wrong section counts HERE (Factuality); a missing citation pattern does NOT (that is Format).

options.label: Mostly accurate
options.description: Mostly accurate (boundary — passes): only a minor imprecision such as rounding or a loose paraphrase; all material claims agree with the REFERENCE ANSWER.

options.label: Completely accurate
options.description: All claims are correct and grounded in the WHO fact sheets, matching the REFERENCE ANSWER, and any cited sections are the correct ones. A correct refusal, when the REFERENCE ANSWER says a refusal is correct, also scores 5.
